title: T12: Shared behavioural conformance corpus for ML500
description: Implements D2 inside the tracer. A language-neutral fixture corpus for naive ML500 that both implementations execute, so the two agree on behaviour and not merely on metadata. Covers the parts of ML500's meaning that live in code rather than in spelling_map.json: identifier word-splitting (Python's WORDS_RE handles camelCase, snake_case and kebab-case), case restoration in the suggested replacement, URL skipping, dotted-name skipping, and which text spans are scanned at all. Scoped to naive ML500 - no exemptions, since those are K1 and are divergent by design.
acceptance_criteria: A committed fixture file both implementations run. Must demonstrably fail when one implementation's word-splitting or case handling is changed and the other's is not. States which behaviours are in scope and which are accepted divergences.

title: F3: Minimal non-mutating just ci
description: Implements the E1 half of D5. Stands up a just ci recipe that can actually fail, before any generated artefact is introduced. Today just lint mutates (justfile:17-18: ruff format . then ruff check --fix .), precommit regenerates docs then git adds them (justfile:64-67), and CI runs only just precommit (ci.yml:37), so CI cannot fail on formatting or doc drift and check-rules-docs (justfile:83) is dead code referenced nowhere.
acceptance_criteria: just ci exists and runs ruff format --check, ruff check --no-fix, and both existing --check generators, none of them mutating. Verified green on main as of 2026-08-28, so it goes in without fallout. Deliberately misformatting a file, or hand-editing a generated doc, makes just ci fail.

title: D7: Document corrections sweep and bead re-sync
description: Instance-level RV0 findings, each evidence-checked. (1) T9: 17 of 19 should be 18 of 19 - at T9's position only ML500 has a TS implementation, K2 is in E3 and nothing orders it earlier. (2) T4: 'require-meta-docs-description enforces its presence for free' is false - the rule is not in configs.recommended (21 rules, not this one) and its default is pattern ^(enforce|require|disallow), which 0 of 19 current summaries match; it needs explicit enabling with pattern '.+'. (3) T4: record the answer to its own open question - eslint-plugin-eslint-plugin 7.6.2 ships 39 rules and none is a rule-name convention rule, and ESLint 10.9.1 accepted the id @ml-lints/ML500 without complaint. (4) T4: typescript-eslint 8.68.0 peers typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0 while current TypeScript is 7.0.2, so a plain install fails with ERESOLVE - pin typescript ^5.9 and say why. (5) T7: good examples fail as specified - the direct translation of ML500's good example fires two @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars errors under eslint:recommended plus @typescript-eslint/recommended, and the Python underscore-prefix trick does not transfer; only exported, fully-used code comes out clean. Python survives via an ignore list (ANN201,RUF100,TC,T201,INP001) and a 15-line PRELUDE at test_rule_examples.py:27-41; T7 specifies no analogue for either. (6) F2: tests/rules/test_ml500_australian_english.py:245 asserts the opposite of F2's acceptance and must be deleted or inverted, and ml500_australian_english.py:68 'return self._SPELLING_MAP or {}' is a second silent-empty path F2 does not close. (7) K1: 'non-JSDoc string literals' is a category error - JSDoc is a comment, not a string literal; the faithful mapping of Python's docstring/string split is 'check all comments including JSDoc, exempt all string literals'. (8) R3: the cited break does not exist - README.md:51 says 'Pin to a specific tag' but the code block that follows has no tag and no git source, and there is no git+https pin anywhere in the repo; the tag change is real but 'most user-visible break' is unsupported. (9) R1/R2: add the .release-please-manifest.json key migration from '.' to packages/py, the root CHANGELOG.md relocation, and the per-component fix for release-please.yml:98 'gh release edit --draft=false'; R2 also names tag_name/pr as the publish gates when the actual gate is release_created at :80. (10) T3: nothing validates the exported manifest against T1's schema - T1 validates the schema against a hand-written example and T3's --check compares the exporter against itself, so the two never meet; add schema validation of the committed manifest. (11) A2: also fix GEMINI.md:42, which cites a just lint-api recipe that does not exist, and the README install section. (12) Re-anchor stale line refs: cli.py:478 is now :481; ml500_australian_english.py:56-60 is :55-56.
acceptance_criteria: All twelve corrections applied to docs/typescript-port.md. Affected beads (T3, T4, T7, T9, F2, K1, R1, R2, R3, A2) re-synced so their acceptance criteria match the amended doc.

title: D6: Confirm the @ml-lints npm scope and hoist the check into E1
description: RV0 framework finding. T4 hardcodes @ml-lints into rule IDs, and T8 checks docUrl against a canonical template derived from it, but T11 - ten tasks later - is the first place the scope is confirmed. That contradicts the delivery principle stated at line 43: put the nastiest external unknown where a rollback costs nothing. Right now the publish is de-risked but the name is not. Verified 2026-08-28: @ml-lints/eslint-plugin returns 404 from the registry, so the package name is free, but scope ownership cannot be determined without authentication and has not been checked.
acceptance_criteria: Scope confirmed claimable, or an alternative name chosen. Doc moves the confirmation into E1 ahead of T4. If the scope is taken, the naming decision is re-founded before T4 rather than after T11.

title: D5: Move a non-mutating just ci into E1 and add a standing failing-capable-check clause
description: RV0 framework finding. just ci does not exist in the justfile today - T10 creates it. Four tasks introduce a generated artefact before then: T2 (vendored spelling map, with precommit auto-staging it), T3 (Python manifest), T6 (TypeScript manifest), T9 (docs, while precommit still regenerates and stages them). T2's sole falsification test is 'hand-editing a vendored copy fails just ci', which cannot be executed at T2 because T10 is three steps later in the DAG. That is the same defect T10 exists to fix, recurring four times in one epic. The framework has no standing invariant that a generated artefact ships with a failing-capable check in the same task that introduces it, so artefacts added after T10 (A1 scaffolding, every future rule) also depend on someone remembering - which GEMINI.md forbids.
acceptance_criteria: Doc moves a minimal non-mutating just ci into E1, ahead of T2, covering ruff format --check, ruff check --no-fix and both existing --check generators (all three verified green on main as of 2026-08-28, so it costs nothing to stand up now). T2, T3, T6 and T9 each gain the clause: adds its --check to just ci, demonstrated by a deliberate hand-edit failing. T10 reduced to adding Node to CI and revoking precommit's auto-stage.

title: D4: Specify shared/categories.json and widen RV1 scope to cover it
description: RV0 instance finding. T1 names shared/categories.json but never says what is in it. T8 validates every category against it, and A1 needs a category-to-block mapping to answer next-free for a category that has no codes yet - per-block next-free is undefined for a new category, because the block is only inferable from codes that already exist. RV1's stated scope is 'T1's schema', singular, so categories.json ships un-gated. Verified: all nine current categories (return-types, type-hygiene, parameter-types, class-shape, scope, data-trust, localisation, testing) are language-neutral, so category is the one drift-checked field that legitimately survives D1.
acceptance_criteria: Doc specifies categories.json fields including a block per category. RV1's remit covers both the manifest schema and categories.json.

title: D3: Re-spec T8 as two gates - toolchain-free metadata and per-language behaviour
description: RV0 framework finding. T8's stated property - reads ONLY the two committed JSON files, so it needs neither toolchain - is exactly what forecloses behavioural conformance. That constraint was chosen for convenience, not because it is the property that decides whether two implementations agree. Depends on D1 (what is shared) and D2 (how behaviour is compared).
acceptance_criteria: T8 split in the doc into a metadata gate (toolchain-free; drift-checks the shared concept field and category, plus the existing structural checks) and a per-language fixture runner. RV3's scope updated to cover both. Both halves retain the must-demonstrably-fail falsification requirement.

title: D2: Specify a shared behavioural conformance mechanism
description: RV0 framework finding. Line 13 promises a machine-checkable guarantee that both implementations agree on what each ML### code means, and the author confirmed behavioural agreement is intended. Nothing in the plan compares behaviour. ML500's meaning lives in Python code, not in the shared JSON: the WORDS_RE camelCase/snake_case splitter (ml500_australian_english.py:46), case restoration (:70-81), URL-span skipping (:85), dotted-name skipping (:89), the docstring-versus-string-literal split, and the message text - the last explicitly deferred by T1 as 'message templates out of v1'. T5's entire acceptance is 'flags const color = 1'. The two implementations can disagree on every one of those and the gate still reports conformance. F1 exists because this hole was spotted for the data file; it is wide open for the algorithm.
acceptance_criteria: Doc specifies a language-neutral fixture format (input source plus expected findings: line, col, code, messageId, data) and where it lives; both implementations run it; the tracer includes an ML500 corpus. Doc states explicitly which behaviours are in scope for v1 and which are accepted divergences.

title: D1: Split manifest concept from per-language summary and suggestion
description: RV0 framework finding. T8 drift-checks summary and suggestion, but only 4 of 19 rules (ML201, ML300, ML500, ML501) have strings that can be byte-identical across languages. The other 15 name Python constructs: NamedTuple, NewType, Mapping, dataclass(frozen=True), dataclasses.replace, Pydantic, patch(new=Mock()). The first TS release is ML500 plus ML501 - two of the four that happen to work - so the gate looks healthy for exactly as long as the tracer lasts, then breaks on the third rule ported. The doc nominates ML400 (Context) and the ML100 family (note after K3) as next; both are in the un-shareable set. The field summary is doing two incompatible jobs: naming the concept (must match, which is what 'ML### names a concept' means) and phrasing the remedy in one language's idiom (cannot match). The schema has one field for both and the only other bucket is not-checked-at-all, where exemptions went.
acceptance_criteria: docs/typescript-port.md amended so the manifest carries a language-neutral concept field that MUST match across manifests, separate from per-language presentation fields. T1's per-rule field list and T8's drift-checked list updated to match. Worked examples for ML400 and ML100 showing both languages, demonstrating the shared field is genuinely writable for a rule whose remedy differs by language.

title: T1: Manifest JSON schema, Pydantic model and categories.json
description: See docs/typescript-port.md#T1. shared/schema/rule-manifest.schema.json plus scripts/manifest_model.py (GEMINI.md mandates Pydantic for file-loaded data) plus shared/categories.json. Per rule: code, concept, category, summary, suggestion, rationale, exemptions?, badExample, goodExamples, docUrl - where concept is the language-neutral statement of what the code means and MUST match across manifests, while summary and suggestion are per-language presentation. Envelope: manifestVersion, language (closed enum), package, version. categories.json carries each category's name and its code block. Deliberately out of v1: message templates, severity, fixability.
acceptance_criteria: Rules sorted by code; serialised with indent=2, sort_keys=True and a trailing newline, because byte-stability is what makes --check work. Schema validates a hand-written ML500 example. Worked concept/summary/suggestion examples for ML400 and ML100 in both languages prove the concept field is writable where the remedy differs. Must survive the question 'what breaks when Rust is added'.
